purpose: Land missions and settlement interactions on the generated worlds. The land_missions probe (src/MNBL.ProceduralWorld/Automation/LandMissionsProbe.cs) reads its world, designated test save and rules from this file; tools/summarize_land_missions.py checks every case below against the run's outputs and writes evidence/gameplay/land-missions.json. A case absent from both worlds is listed as absent, never passed. A failure found by a run or the review is added to regressions with what now guards it.

worldB.use: only for a case world A lacks

stockMissingPatterns: ^Voice object for text id is not found:

cases.what: One field battle on each battle class present in world A (the resolver's classes of the compiled biomes and face terrain: open, woodland, steppe, rock, cold, desert, wetland; every cell with a land sample counts, as the battle map classes it), one of them a substituted class (woodland and rock fight on Plain scenes, cold on Steppe scenes: no installed battle scene is Forest, Mountain or Snow); a class A lacks is fought in world B, and a class both lack is absent. Each battle: the player's party at a sample point of a cell of that class, a lord party of the next culture present beside it (its kingdom at war for the battle, peace made after, the party put back where it was), the official encounter and its attack option; only those two parties fight, in a land map event; the scene the engine opens is the one the generated battle-index map names for the patch, and MMR-42's guard made its own observation of this battle's choice and agreed; deployment finished; every agent spawned on the scene's navigation mesh inside its boundaries; the mission ended through Mission.OnEndMissionResult (whose installed implementation leaves the battle by retreating); the party returns within the vanilla encounter radius bound, on land, on valid navigation.
One field battle at a crossing: the player's party on a Bridge or Fording sample point of a crossing cell; checked as a field battle.

One field battle the player leaves by retreating (Mission.RetreatMission, as the retreat order does), checked as a field battle; the battle is left to the enemy: the player's side did not win and the enemy party remains, with healthy troops.

A town entered through the official encounter (the town menu): its center (town_streets) opens the settlement's mapped center scene; a notable or merchant there is spoken to (MissionConversationLogic.StartConversation: the conversation's agent and its first line); its tavern interior opens through the location encounter (TownEncounter.CreateAndOpenMissionController, as the center's tavern door does) with the mapped tavern scene; the player leaves through the menu's leave path at its gate (where it entered), on land, on valid navigation.

A castle entered (the castle menu; the castle is first given to the player's clan, recorded as diagnostic setup, so its gates open without a guard dialogue): its courtyard (take_a_walk_around_the_castle) opens the mapped center scene; the player leaves through the menu at its gate (where it entered), on land, on valid navigation.
A village entered (the village menu): its center (village_center) opens the mapped village scene; the player leaves through the menu at its gate (where it entered), on land, on valid navigation.

One infested hideout cleared: outside the hideout model's night hours (campaign time runs past them if needed: sneaking in by night opens the stealth ambush mission instead), the player's party at the hideout's gate and its assault option, the troop selection it opens answered with the selection it offers (as Done without changes); the hideout mission opens the hideout's mapped hideout_center scene; bandits fall only in the controller's fight phases and the boss only in the boss fight; the boss's dialogue answered through its own battle option; the mission won; the hideout is no longer infested and the party returns to the gate on valid navigation.

One siege assault with deployment: the player besieges a hostile castle (the outside menu's besiege option; the castle farthest from its own kingdom's lord parties, since a relief's encounter stops the camp's preparation), the camp's own preparation observed as campaign time runs for siegeObserveHours (its rate per hour and a time series of the menu, the siege, the camp's progress and the player's map event recorded), then brought to siegeCompletionFrom as diagnostic setup (recorded: at the installed rate the camp needs about four days, in which the garrison sallies out, a stock mechanic not retested here) and completed by the engine's own tick; the assault (menu_siege_strategies_lead_assault) opens the settlement's mapped center scene in its siege level with deployment finished; the assault is broken off (Mission.OnEndMissionResult) and the siege lifted through the menu; the party returns on valid navigation.

One party defeat leading to capture and escape: the player's party attacks a stronger hostile party and loses in the mission (every agent of the player's team falls, the main agent knocked out; the mission, ended by its own logic, is left as the leave button leaves it); the campaign takes the player prisoner; the escape (EndCaptivityAction.ApplyByEscape, as the captivity's escape applies it) frees the party near its captor (the installed release teleports it out of the encounter radius twice: within 2 x 1.25 x the encounter model's land radius of the captor's position), on land, on valid navigation.

Every culture present in world A shows complete troop and hero gear in mission: each human agent of the battles carries body armour and a weapon, every equipped item's meshes exist (MetaMesh.GetCopy: a crafted weapon's piece meshes, else the item's MultiMeshName), and each culture present is seen with both troops and a hero (a lord party of each culture fights; one in a settlement leaves it first, recorded as setup).
Every generated settlement's location scenes meet the mission scene contracts and the engine finds each scene file (MMR-42's audit, live); every settlement entered opened its mapped scene.

Encyclopedia names: every generated settlement, clan, kingdom and lord has a resolved name and encyclopedia link (no unresolved {=...} or {VARIABLE}), with an encyclopedia page that accepts it; every location menu the cases opened had its options.

No missing asset and valid spawns in the cases' missions: no engine log line during a case names a generated object or a scene the case opened as missing, and every other missing line is of a stock kind the scenario file names (stockMissingPatterns); no engine assert fired (Debug.DebugManager wrapper with a canary); in every mission opened, every active human agent stands on a face of the scene's navigation mesh and inside the mission's boundaries.
No game and every tracked static at its baseline at the start and at the end.

regressions.failure: Every agent was counted as incompletely geared: each crafted weapon (swords, spears, axes, javelins of every culture) was recorded as having no mesh name.
regressions.cause: A crafted weapon names no ItemObject.MultiMeshName; it is drawn from its WeaponDesign's pieces, each with its own CraftingPiece.MeshName.
regressions.fix: A crafted weapon's meshes are its valid, non-empty pieces' meshes (each checked with MetaMesh.GetCopy); a crafted weapon without one, or another item without a MultiMeshName, is still missing.

regressions.failure: The battles meant for battania, khuzait, sturgia and the woodland, rock and cold classes fought a sea raider party: no lord party of those cultures was found.
regressions.cause: The enemy had to be outside any settlement; every lord party of those cultures was resting in a town or castle at the save.
regressions.fix: A lord party in a settlement not under siege is taken too (parties on the map first), leaving it through LeaveSettlementAction.ApplyForParty, recorded as setup (enemyLeftSettlement).

regressions.failure: The hideout's attack option held but was disabled after campaign time ran to night (CampaignTime.IsNightTime), so the case stopped before the mission.
regressions.cause: Sneaking in is enabled only in the hideout model's attack hours (HideoutModel.CanAttackHideoutStartTime to EndTime), narrower than the campaign's night; outside them the frontal assault is enabled instead. Both open a troop selection (MenuContext.OpenTroopSelection) before the mission.
regressions.fix: The case takes whichever of attack and assault is enabled (each option's enabled state and tooltip now recorded with the menus) and answers the troop selection with the selection it offers, through a handler that passes every other menu call on.

regressions.failure: After 96 campaign hours the camp's preparation stood at 0.028 and the menu was the encounter: the camp was never prepared.
regressions.cause: The camp builds at the installed rate (SiegeEventModel.GetConstructionProgressPerHour: 0.0106 per hour for a 150-troop party, about 94 campaign hours), and the castle's garrison sallies out against the camp within hours (run 17928: a SallyOut map event at 3.65 hours, garrison 100 against 114); the camp does not build while its party is in a map event, and the probe's fast-forward kept time running.
regressions.fix: The besieged castle is the one farthest from its own kingdom's lord parties; the camp's rate per hour, a time series every half hour and any interruption (the map event's type and parties, or the siege ending) are recorded, and an interruption stops the case at once. The camp's own preparation is observed for siegeObserveHours, then brought to siegeCompletionFrom (diagnostic setup, recorded with the observed progress and the hours a natural preparation needs) and completed by the engine's tick. Sally-outs are stock mechanics the ticket does not retest.

regressions.failure: After the player's defeat the mission never tore down (the case timed out); the capture only followed when the game was ended.
regressions.cause: A mission whose logic reports its end (MissionEnded set by CheckMissionEnded) still waits for the player's leave, which calls Mission.EndMission; the probe skipped its end (and its screenshot) for an ended mission.
regressions.fix: The case's end is called whenever the mission is still current, recording whether it had ended itself; the screenshot is taken either way.

regressions.failure: The game stopped responding (no CPU, no dialog) as the hideout boss's conversation opened, in runs 25280 and 17928; each run was lost from there.
regressions.cause: Run 17928 hung before the probe's first dialogue step (its checkpoint never ran): the engine hung opening the conversation. The probe had killed every enemy agent every half second through the controller's cutscene before the boss fight (HideoutMissionController._hideoutMissionState CutSceneBeforeBossFight, then ConversationBetweenLeaders), which no player can do. Run 25280 also ended the conversation on its first frame and called the battle mode itself, where the installed dialogue queues it for the conversation's end.
regressions.fix: Bandits fall only in the controller's fight phases and the boss (_bossAgent) only in the boss fight; each phase change is recorded and checkpointed. The boss's dialogue is answered as a click answers it (ConversationManager.DoOption on the battle option, the duel when the battle is not clickable), then continued until it closes, each step checkpointed. The hideout runs last, after world B (world A reloaded for it). Run 48860: the four phases in order, the battle option chosen, the mission won.

regressions.failure: With lords in settlements allowed, battania, khuzait and sturgia still fought bandits: none of their lord parties passed the filter.
regressions.cause: Every lord party of those cultures owns ships (War Sails gives most northern lords a fleet; run 17928's census: battania 23 of 40 lords, khuzait 11 of 19, sturgia 16 of 25, the others in settlements without a party), and the filter excluded any party with ships.
regressions.fix: A party with ships fights on land like any other when it is not at sea (setup.enemyShips recorded; a battle that becomes a naval map event fails the case); a fallback to bandits records a census of the culture's lords by the first filter each fails (setup.lordCensus).

regressions.failure: No crossing was found, and the steppe and wetland classes were absent, with cells sampled every fifth cell (198 land cells).
regressions.cause: Bridge and Fording faces are narrow; a stride of five cells skipped them, and small class areas with them.
regressions.fix: Every cell is sampled (cellStride 1); the cells with a Bridge or Fording sample are counted (terrain.crossingCells), and the crossing battle stands on such a sample point.

regressions.failure: Only field battles checked where the party came back: the town, castle, village, hideout, siege and capture rows checked its navigation alone, and nothing judged a return 3.82 map units from the siege's start (run 48860).
regressions.cause: The return rows were cut to the navigation row for every case but the field battles, and the probe recorded no expected return point for them.
regressions.fix: Each case records where its installed path puts the party (the gate it entered; the siege camp for the assault's return; the captor's position, where PlayerCaptivity.EndCaptivityInternal releases the party) and is checked against it with the vanilla land bound, on land as before, on valid navigation.

regressions.failure: No check read an agent's spawn position: a main agent under the terrain or outside the mission's boundaries would have passed.
regressions.cause: The mission record kept the main agent's position and terrain samples, which no check read.
regressions.fix: After deployment (or readiness) every active human agent's position is checked on the scene's navigation mesh (the Vec3 form of Scene.GetNavMeshFaceIndex, as mission code calls it, at the agent's height or half a metre below or above it for a seated or mounted agent) and inside the mission's boundaries.

regressions.failure: A missing-asset line that named neither a generated object nor an opened scene was only tallied, so an unknown missing mesh or texture would have passed.
regressions.cause: The log window failed a case only on lines naming the world's prefix or an opened scene.
regressions.fix: Every missing line is of a stock kind the scenario file names (stockMissingPatterns: shader variants compiled on first use, unvoiced dialogue lines) or fails the case (log.otherMissingCount).

regressions.failure: The player's hero and the crew the probe adds counted for their culture, and world B's battles counted for world A's cultures, so a culture of A could pass without one of its lords fighting.
regressions.cause: The culture tally counted every human agent of every battle, in one tally for both worlds.
regressions.fix: The tally counts only the agents of other parties than the player's (their origin's party), and world B keeps its own tally (culturesB).

regressions.failure: Run 17928's gear battles were four-party battles: the lord parties parked at the open cell by earlier battles joined as the player's allies, and the cases passed.
regressions.cause: Each enemy was moved beside the player and left there; the battle's parties were recorded but not checked.
regressions.fix: Only the player's party and the enemy may fight (else the case fails), and the enemy is put back where it was (into its settlement if it left one) after the battle.

regressions.failure: The retreat's rows restated the probe's own input: nothing showed that the battle was left to the enemy, and Mission.OnEndMissionResult, which the field battles call, itself ends by retreating.
regressions.cause: The map event's outcome was not recorded before the encounter was finished.
regressions.fix: Every field battle records its outcome before the encounter is finished (the map event's state and winner, the enemy's state); the retreat requires that the player's side did not win and the enemy remains with healthy troops.

regressions.failure: The guard row could be met by an earlier battle's observation: field.open and the retreat open the same scene at the same cell.
regressions.cause: MissionScenePatches.LastOpening returns the last observation of a scene's name.
regressions.fix: The battle takes the guard's observations made since its own encounter began (MissionScenePatches.Observed before and after) and requires one of them for its scene.

regressions.failure: The siege row read as if the camp had prepared in 2.6 campaign hours, and a camp that never built would have passed once advanced.
regressions.cause: The row reported the total hours and the prepared flag only.
regressions.fix: The rows state the camp's own progress, its rate and the hours a natural preparation needs, require the observed progress to be above zero, and name the advance as diagnostic setup.

regressions.failure: The game stopped responding as the town's tavern mission opened, right after the first spawn check that needed a fallback lookup; the run was lost from there.
regressions.cause: The fallback used the Vec2 form of Scene.GetNavMeshFaceIndex with its first flag set. Installed code calls that form only on the campaign map, where the flag is the map's land region (CampaignVec2.IsOnLand); mission code calls only the Vec3 form.
regressions.fix: The spawn check uses only the Vec3 form, at the agent's height or half a metre below or above it.

regressions.failure: The spawn check failed stock agents: in the town 2 center agents and 10 tavern agents, and in the siege 1 troop, stood off the navigation mesh.
regressions.cause: Seated agents (ChairUsePoint), the tavern's musician (PlayMusicPoint) and agents on scene geometry stand where the stock scene puts them, off its navigation mesh; the check took every agent off the mesh for a bad spawn.
regressions.fix: An agent off the mesh that uses a scene object, sits, or stands on a machine or other scene geometry (Agent.GetSteppedMachine, GetSteppedRootEntity) or on the terrain itself within half a metre (a gap in the stock scene's mesh: run 43696's siege troop) is recorded apart with what supports it; an agent off the mesh with nothing under it, or the main agent off the mesh, still fails.

regressions.failure: The escape released the party 1.17 to 1.19 map units from its captor, beyond the single encounter-radius teleport's 0.625.
regressions.cause: PlayerCaptivity.EndCaptivityInternal puts the party at its captor and teleports it out of the encounter radius; the release's OnHeroPrisonerReleased listener then calls PlayerEncounter.ProtectPlayerSide, which teleports it again from there. Time was stopped (run 35564), so the party did not move by itself.
regressions.fix: The capture's bound is the installed one: 2 x 1.25 x EncounterModel.NeededMaximumLandDistanceForEncounteringMobileParty (recorded as encounterRadius) from the captor's position, measured with time stopped right after the escape.
